title: Source-qualified TEST JUSTIFY-D1 triangle area equality
subject: TEST
scope_summary: AUTHORED TEST derived from existing IMO-G9-ORIGINAL-PRACTICE-003, with source-intake ALTITUDE_WORDING_CLARITY hold. Main D1 W: justify equal area of two triangles sharing 12 cm base and 7 cm perpendicular altitudes despite displaced peaks. Core1A 10×4 worked, Core1B 10×3 misconception and 8 cm unequal-height boundary, Core2B converse height from equal area 36 and base 12. No original SOF source rights, independent review or release.

conventions.statement: Use the same specified segment AB as the base in both triangles.
Altitude is the perpendicular distance to the straight line through base AB, not a slanted edge.

capabilities.action: Justify why two triangles with a shared base and equal perpendicular altitudes have equal areas despite different slanted sides.
capabilities.success_criterion: Identify a valid base-height area warrant, calculate both 12×7/2 = 42 cm², falsify shared-base-only reasoning using unequal heights, and reverse area to height in a genuinely changed task.

entry_assumptions: Triangle area is half base times perpendicular height.

microtopics.inferential_jump: Decide whether the equal base and perpendicular altitude facts license equal triangle areas even when apex positions differ.

teaching_path.action: Declare chosen base and perpendicular altitude as the area-determining pair.
teaching_path.why_valid: A triangle occupies half the area of an associated base-height parallelogram.

teaching_path.action: Solve a DIFFERENT triangle: base 10 cm and perpendicular altitude 4 cm.
teaching_path.why_valid: A=10×4/2=20 cm² from the actual perpendicular height.

teaching_path.action: Slide the worked apex sideways while keeping its height 4 cm, then verify unchanged area.
teaching_path.why_valid: The formula has the same base and perpendicular height after translation parallel to the baseline.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A shifted apex or unequal slanted sides prove triangle areas differ.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A peak slides sideways over the same 10 cm base, staying 3 cm above its line. A student claims its area grows because the slanted side is longer. Is this warranted?
misconceptions.repair: Use the 3 cm perpendicular height, not the changing slanted side: both triangle areas remain 10×3/2 = 15 cm².

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Equal base lengths alone prove areas are equal.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: With common base 8 cm, altitudes 5 cm and 4 cm differ. Must the areas match?
misconceptions.repair: No; 8×5/2=20 and 8×4/2=16 cm². The perpendicular height condition matters.

exit_task.prompt: Changed exit: two triangles share a 9 cm base and both peaks are at perpendicular distance 6 cm. Justify equal areas and calculate them.

reasoning: Both heights to its line are perpendicular and 6 cm.
Area A=bh/2 is therefore 27 cm² for both.
answer.check: Determinants for vertices (0,0),(9,0),(2,6) and (0,0),(9,0),(7,6) both give 27.

questions.stem: Triangles ABC and ABD share the straight base AB, 12 cm long. Imagine extending the straight line through A and B beyond both endpoints if needed. From C, the shortest distance to that line, measured at a right angle (90°), is 7 cm. The shortest distance from D to the same line, also at a right angle, is 7 cm. The peaks C and D lie at different sideways positions. Must the triangles have equal areas? Give a mathematical reason and find both areas.
conditions: AB is the same 12 cm base for ABC and ABD.
The given 7 cm distances from C and D are each the shortest 90° distances to the straight line containing AB, extended beyond the segment if necessary.
Peaks are horizontally displaced; slanted edge lengths may differ.
Authored practice TEST candidate; source-quality ALTITUDE_WORDING_CLARITY review pending.

answer.summary: Yes. Both areas are 42 cm² because each has b=12 cm and perpendicular h=7 cm in A=bh/2.
reasoning: A chosen triangle base and its perpendicular altitude determine area.
Both triangles have the same 12 cm base and 7 cm perpendicular altitude.
A=12×7/2=42 cm² for each; horizontal peak displacement does not change that formula.

reasoning_route.action: Identify common base AB and both perpendicular altitudes.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Distances were measured perpendicular to the same baseline.
reasoning_route.output: The two relevant input pairs match.

reasoning_route.action: Justify equal area by the area relation A=bh/2 for both triangles.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The product of matched base and perpendicular altitude is the same even for differently placed apexes.
Both applications give 42 cm²; a determinant check is independent.

answer.check: A=(0,0),B=(12,0),C=(2,7),D=(10,7): both determinant areas are |12×7|/2=42 cm².

scaffolds.text: What is the shared base? Locate the two 7 cm shortest distances measured at 90° to the straight base line, rather than following either slanted edge.
Recall a triangle-area relation involving a base and its perpendicular distance. What must you check about the measurements before you can use that relation to support or reject an area comparison?
After committing your own reasoning, calculate each area separately using the stated base and perpendicular distance, then check your conclusion and square-unit labels.

questions.stem: CHANGED CONVERSE: two triangles share base 12 cm and EACH has area 36 cm². Neither perpendicular altitude is stated. Use an area relation to determine each missing perpendicular altitude and justify why the heights agree.
conditions: Both have the same positive 12 cm base.
Wholly authored converse transfer TEST; no organizer item used.

answer.summary: Both perpendicular altitudes are 6 cm, because h=2A/b=2×36/12.
reasoning: Triangle area A=bh/2 holds for each.
Both have A=36 and b=12, so h=6 cm for each; 12×6/2 verifies area 36 cm².

reasoning_route.action: Identify each A=36 cm² and b=12 cm.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The values are given for both triangles.

reasoning_route.action: Reverse the relation to h=2A/b, then infer both heights are 6 cm.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The same positive base and area determine the same perpendicular altitude.
This reproduces the stated area for both triangles.
